besluite.fout: An English-style cleft ('dit is die vel ... wat vibreer') with two stacked relative clauses makes a Grade 4 reader stumble.
besluite.rede: The plain main-clause order says the same thing (same part, same action, contrast with the guitar string intact) and reads more easily, and the next sentence still follows from it.

besluite.fout: 'die vel' has no antecedent here; the drum is mentioned but its skin is not, so a child can read it as their own skin.
besluite.rede: Naming the drum adds no new fact, since the drum is already in the paragraph, and it removes a real ambiguity; no protected wording is touched.
